steps.what: Pose an economics question and establish the discussion's terms
Invite contributions, probe economic reasoning and moderate disagreement
Compare arguments aloud and clarify remaining misconceptions

tasks.design: Keep the discussion with the teacher. A native {LMS} discussion board is useful for a different asynchronous activity, but does not remove the teacher's live questioning, moderation or spoken synthesis here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Participation and economic misconceptions emerge during the exchange.
tasks.enabler_now: No technology change removes a present step in this live-discussion boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising when a plausible argument rests on an unstated economic assumption.
tasks.human_edge: Invite quieter students and challenge reasoning without humiliating anyone.
tasks.altitude: The teacher's classroom responsibilities and time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Use questions that expose causal assumptions.

evidence.claim: Live discussion facilitation depends on contingent student contributions and teacher judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is the live discussion, not separate lesson-material preparation or assessed marking. No attendance entry, discussion transcript, grade or written follow-up is assumed for an ordinary ungraded discussion; verify locally before adding any. No record write or send is hidden in the spoken steps.

Inputs are the teacher's current lesson and students' spoken contributions; no structured feed is required. Existing lesson materials remain human-prepared in their own task. Native discussion-board configuration was considered but would change the activity rather than save its live work.
No deployment or additional upkeep, so incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether a particular discussion is assessed and requires a separate grade record.
research_questions: Are any discussion records actually kept and used, rather than merely possible?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 100 hours remain live teacher work. Even with an existing board, questioning, moderation and spoken synthesis remain; there is no assumed transcription baseline to cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise student teaching, internships and research

steps.what: Read the student's submitted work and applicable supervision requirements
Discuss progress, research choices and difficulties with the student
Write specific comments on the student's existing work submission

loop.purpose: Express the supervisor's already chosen feedback clearly
loop.input: Student passages and supervisor-entered comments and agreed next actions
loop.output: Draft comments anchored to the supplied passages
loop.check: Supervisor checks economic meaning, tone, passage references and every proposed action
loop.stop: Missing passage support or a new evaluative judgement returns the comment to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed form cannot express the relationship between a particular argument and its methodological weakness

steps.what: Check the final feedback and intended student recipient
Release the checked feedback to the student

tasks.design: Use the existing {LMS} submission and feedback editor first; only if permitted and useful, add a bounded drafting aid to comments the supervisor already makes. Keep reading, discussion and final feedback judgement with the teacher, and retain the small native student-release action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual supervision comments need context that a generic feedback template lacks.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting tool can work from the supervisor's chosen comments and student passages.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing research validity, teaching practice and an internship's educational value.
tasks.human_edge: Notice weak evidence and negotiate a feasible next step with the student.
tasks.altitude: A little less phrasing work; no transfer of supervisory or assessment authority.

reach.learn: Distinguish actionable feedback from unsupported judgement.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes; this supports drafting capability, not a measured supervision saving.

assumptions: Boundary covers recurring supervision including comments on work the student actually submits; no extra progress log, grading import or internship-employer report is invented. Other assessment tasks remain separate.

Student supplies submission identifier, text and version in {LMS}; institution supplies supervision requirements. Teacher first captures substantive comments during the retained s3 work. Missing or confidential material is read and commented on manually; no automatic summary of an unseen submission.

Of s3's 20 hours, 5 are routine wording and restructuring; 15 remain for first capture, passage selection, correction and unsupported-comment fallback. Native save time is included and unchanged. Student release is a real external handoff, not an author save.
Approval a1 binds final feedback text, submission version and student recipient after s4; any edit invalidates it. No model assigns grades or decides satisfactory progress.
unknowns: Whether confidential student work may enter an approved drafting service.
How much present comment writing repeats phrasing rather than develops the teacher's judgement.
research_questions: Does the native feedback editor already remove the five hours of phrasing work?

already_counted.description: First capture, passage selection, meaning corrections and manual fallback in feedback writing

incremental.description: Maintain feedback instructions and check draft failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact final feedback text, submission version and student recipient checked in s4; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 5 hours of phrasing removed, minus 1 upkeep = 4. Cautious case is original research feedback whose wording itself develops the evaluation: all 20 writing hours remain, the drafting aid is not deployed and adds no upkeep, giving zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Hear the student's question during the scheduled office hour
Explain course concepts and help the student work through difficulties

tasks.design: Keep regular office-hour availability and individual help with the teacher. Test the existing {CALENDAR} arrangement only if there is actual repeated booking work; do not claim a saving from a recurring slot set once per term.
tasks.previous_blocker: The student needs a response to their own confusion, not simply an available appointment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calendars already support recurring availability; their runtime is not teacher labour.
tasks.still_hard: Discovering why the student cannot apply a familiar economic concept.
tasks.human_edge: Build enough trust for the student to reveal a misunderstanding.
tasks.altitude: Office-hour time and teaching responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: A recurring calendar slot does not automate the individual explanation delivered in office hours.

assumptions: Boundary is holding recurring office hours. Availability is already published; no repeated slot setup, appointment triage, attendance record, case log or follow-up email is assumed. Ordinary spoken help requires none of those by default.

Student supplies the question verbally and teacher uses existing course materials; no machine-readable student profile is assumed. If an actual lookup, written recommendation or referral occurs, decompose its real work separately as in 5996 rather than treating it as conversation.

5996 and this task can describe the same advising encounter. A roll-up must allocate that encounter to one owner, not add both estimates; these are task alternatives, not duplicated actions with shared ids.
No new tool, capture or upkeep, so incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether office hours actually involve repeated appointment handling or required written advice.
research_questions: What work occurs between students beyond remaining available?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 100 hours remain availability and personal help. A cautious case with more difficult student questions also removes no present step; calendar setup is not inflated into a recurring baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise on curricula and career choices

steps.what: Explore the student's academic interests, constraints and career questions
Look up current curriculum requirements and relevant career information
Discuss choices, trade-offs and appropriate next contacts with the student
Write the requested advice and reference links for the student
Check the final advice, links and intended student recipient
Send the checked advice to the student

tasks.design: Configure bookmarks and programme filters in the existing {LMS}/{DOCS} catalogue, retaining interpretation of prerequisites and career fit. Use an {EMAIL} snippet only for the introduction and reference-link layout of written advice already requested, then check its meaning and recipient before the small native send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Curriculum information is distributed while career recommendations remain personal.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved views and email snippets reduce navigation and repeated layout without interpreting the student's prospects.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling uncertain career aims with academic and personal constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Help the student make a choice without pretending to predict their career.
tasks.altitude: The teacher spends slightly less time finding source pages and retains every advice decision.

reach.learn: Know referral boundaries and current qualification requirements.

evidence.claim: Saved catalogue views and email snippets can reduce repeated navigation and formatting without deciding an individual's advice.

assumptions: Boundary includes curriculum/career advising and written follow-up where students actually request it. The 7-hour writing share is an explicit typical-work hypothesis to confirm, not a new universal advice log; if advice is wholly oral, remove that work and re-estimate the task.

Curriculum owner produces programme, academic year, module identifier, prerequisite text and current page link; career service maintains resource title, link and update date. Teacher verifies the current source in s2 and manually finds absent information within its retained 12 hours; no free structured student profile or eligibility calculation.

Native filters remove 3 hours of page navigation from s2's 15. A fixed introduction/link layout removes only 0.7 of s4's 7; the 6.3 remaining hours contain first capture of the personal advice and manual wording. No model selects careers. Ordinary draft saves are included and retained.

Approval a1 binds exact email text, links and student address after s5; edits void approval. If the same encounter is counted under office hours 5991, roll-up chooses one task boundary instead of adding both.
unknowns: How often a written follow-up is currently requested.
Whether current bookmarks already remove the navigation work.
research_questions: Which curriculum lookups require unpublished departmental clarification rather than searchable pages?

already_counted.description: Source currency checks and manual lookup fallback

incremental.description: Refresh source links and advice snippet

approvals.approved_version: Final email text, reference links and student address checked in s5; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 3 navigation hours and 0.7 layout hours, minus 0.5 upkeep = 3.2. Cautious case has programme exceptions requiring the full 15 lookup hours; the existing written follow-up still loses 0.7 layout hours, minus 0.5 upkeep = 0.2. No send or author-save saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Live economics teaching, supervision and individual advice stay with the teacher; modest gains concern feedback phrasing and source navigation.
reach: Work with teaching assistants on supervision feedback
Refer specialist career questions to a career adviser
skills_to_grow: Check generated comments against student passages
Distinguish student guidance from formal assessment
role.ambitious_version: Offer clearer supervision feedback while preserving personal economic reasoning and career guidance.
